actual.companyIdValues: 2, 3 and 4 across all 116 rows of the 574/2026 feed — NOT 574, and not any other real company id. These are the same small numbers that appear as `sourceId` on article rows. See AE-M4.

mismatches.status: LIVE — backend-side, nothing this repo can fix
mismatches.expected: The organiser company id — the key that relates an event to its releases. repository.ts loadEventRecord passes it to fetchEventReleases(compId, year).
mismatches.impact: No event in this app can show a single press release. AE-RELEASES itself is perfectly healthy — 574/2026 returns 116 rows — there is simply no value to pass it. The whole release-feed path is dead at the first hop.
mismatches.fix: Backend must populate compId, or expose an events endpoint that returns the organiser. Raise with the API team; there is no frontend workaround short of hardcoding a mapping.

mismatches.expected: An array of organiser companies, repeated once per release — types.ts: "up to 168 identical entries on one event. mapEvent collapses them." The dedupe is the reason the mapped result is small enough to cache.
mismatches.impact: Event.companies is always []. `mapEventCompany` never runs, so no organiser name, logo or URL is ever produced. The dedupe in mapEvent() is a no-op, and the 168-fold-repetition rationale behind it no longer describes anything on the wire.
mismatches.fix: Backend. Keep the dedupe — it costs nothing and is correct if the data returns.

mismatches.status: LIVE — needs a decision from the API team before any code changes
mismatches.actual: 7 events, all future-dated (2026-09-16 to 2026-12-02), all publish="y". Page 2 is empty at any pageSize.
mismatches.impact: The endpoint now behaves as an UPCOMING-EVENTS feed rather than an archive. Two consequences here: the events list shows 7 rows, and because repository.ts resolves a single event by filtering the list (AE-M5), only those 7 ids resolve — any historical event id is now a 404.
mismatches.openQuestion: Is this an intentional backend change or data loss? The public site's capture recorded the same drop on the same day. Worth one question to the API team before anyone re-sizes the paging or drops the cache design — the current code is correct-but-oversized, which is the safe direction to be wrong in.

mismatches.expected: `companyId: number | null` — the company the release is filed against, matching the {companyId} in the request path.
mismatches.actual: Values 2, 3 and 4 across all 116 rows of the 574/2026 feed. It does not echo 574 and it is not any real company id — these are the same small numbers that appear as `sourceId` on article rows (2 = ACN Newswire, 3 = JCN Newswire).
mismatches.impact: A field named companyId carries a source id. Nothing reads it today, so nothing is broken — but anyone unifying the article and event shapes will reasonably assume it joins to a company and it will not.
mismatches.fix: Rename in the type to reflect what it carries (`sourceId`), or confirm the intent with the API team. Note this is the SAME confusion as AP-M4, where the `Cid` query parameter on /api/Articles also behaves as a source id — two separate endpoints making the same substitution suggests a backend-wide naming problem, not two typos.

mismatches.status: LIVE — backend-side, already documented in this repo
mismatches.expected: endpoints.ts already says it 500s and that repository.ts filters the list instead.
mismatches.actual: CONFIRMED still 500, now on the current id set (1104) as well as the historical ids originally recorded. Same EF Core 'Companies' column error.
mismatches.impact: The list-and-filter workaround in loadEventRecord is still required. Combined with AE-M3, that workaround is now also what limits event lookup to 7 ids.

mismatches.expected: Offsetless date-only midnights. map-event.ts stamps WIRE_OFFSET = '+08:00' and pushes endDate to 23:59:59, because a browser would otherwise read the value in the visitor's own timezone and show an event on the 16th as the 15th.
mismatches.actual: CONFIRMED unchanged — "2026-09-16T00:00:00" on all 7 rows, no offset, no Z.
mismatches.impact: The +08:00 stamp is still needed and still correct. It remains a display-honesty patch over data the API does not carry, not a fact the API states.

mismatches.expected: types.ts: "A bare filename. The serving path for these is not known — see ./media.ts."
mismatches.actual: media.ts already resolves it: `eventImageUrl()` returns `${SITE_BASE}/eventimages/{filename}`. The path IS known; the comment contradicts the code next to it. Filenames confirmed bare on all 7 rows (e.g. "2026WBE160.jpg").
mismatches.impact: None functionally. Worth correcting so nobody re-investigates a solved question.

mismatches.expected: `publish` is a "y"/"n" flag; isPublished() filters on it. 816 of 839 were "y". `lid` is "2" on all events — "No variation, so nothing to model."
mismatches.actual: publish = "y" on all 7; lid = "2" on all 7. The filter now removes nothing.
mismatches.impact: None. Keep both — the filter costs nothing and the fields still exist.

verdict.endpointHealth: DEGRADED — AE-LIST returns 200 but with a drastically reduced result set and no organiser data; AE-DETAIL still 500s; AE-RELEASES is healthy but unreachable in practice.
verdict.shapeFidelity: Both working endpoints match their declared shapes exactly. Every problem on this page is a DATA problem, not a shape problem — which is the opposite of the article endpoints.
blockers: No event can show its press releases (AE-M1) — compId is null on every row
No event has an organiser (AE-M2) — companies[] is empty on every row
Only 7 event ids resolve (AE-M3) — every historical event is gone from the wire
verdict.fixableHere: Nothing of substance. AE-M4 and AE-M7 are type/comment corrections; the three blockers are all upstream.
verdict.nextStep: This page is the one that needs the API team before it needs code. Ask three questions: is the 839 → 7 drop intentional, will compId be repopulated, and is /api/Events/{id} on the fix list.
